39025.question_text: ''O happy torment'' is an example of
39025.explanation:
An oxymoron is a figure of speech in which two contradictory or opposing words or ideas are combined to create a striking expression.

“O happy torment” brings together “happy” (a positive feeling) and “torment” (a painful or negative experience), which are opposites.

39027.explanation:

  • "Who doesn’t love a holiday?"

  • "Isn’t it obvious?"
